newsitem.title: USA: U.S. dollar may "creep up" further vs yen - Bergsten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar may "creep up" further vs yen - Bergsten.

text.p: The dollar may raise further against the yen because the U.S. economy is strong and Japan's is quite weak, Fred Bergsten, director of the Institute of International Economics, said on Monday.

"I think the dollar may continue to creep up a little more," Bergsten said on Reuters Financial Television, adding that "the U.S. is by far the strongest economy of the major countries, the Japanese economy is quite weak, the contrast between the two continues to push the dollar up."
He warned that at present levels, the Japanese trade surplus is going to shoot up again over the next year or two.
He said that a jump in the Japanese surplus will lead to a renewed trade friction between the United States and Japan.
"Already the seeds are being sown for a big, renewed trade clash between the United Sates and Japan," he said.
Bergsten said he believed the Japanese strategy was to weaken the yen and thus strengthen their trade surplus because "they don't see any other way of getting out of their current economic weakness."
He said this was the wrong approach and Japan should be making structural reforms in its economy and stimulating domestic demand.

However, he said that following the U.S. elections, he expected the reelected Clinton administration and Congress to get together and make a deal to balance the budget over the next three or four years.

"That in turn will mean much lower U.S. interest rates, that in turn will bring the dollar down," he said, adding that by the end of this year, the "dollar will begin to plane off and maybe even come down a bit."
